chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Hamza, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no potion that a servant swallows that is more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than the potion of anger that he swallows when it churns in his heart, either through patience or through forbearance.'
ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved act of suppressing anger to Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the internal discipline of anger suppression to a supreme act of worship, describing the swallowed rage as a 'potion' more beloved to Allah than other deeds. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and *sabr* (patience) as active spiritual struggles that purify the heart, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of the 'strong man' who controls himself in anger. The metaphor of a 'potion' suggests that enduring the sting of anger yields a spiritual remedy and divine reward, aligning with the concept of *Jihad al-Nafs* (struggle against the self).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Musna Al Hannat, from Abu Hamza having said:

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from the potions swallowed by the servant more beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic than the potion of anger swallowed during repelling it in his heart, either by patience of by forbearance’.
en.sarwar: 13. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from Muthanna al-Hannat from abu Hamza who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once said to me, ‘The swallowing of a servant (of Allah) of no other drop is more beloved to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, than the drop (feeling) of anger when it runs around in his heart, and he swallows it by means of patience and forbearance.’”
